cex-cm02-nonunique-flow-for-a-continuous.title: "Continuity of the force map alone does not give unique motions: two distinct Newtonian motions through one datum for $F=m\\sqrt{|x_1|}\\,e_1$"
cex-cm02-nonunique-flow-for-a-continuous.physical_scope: "A refutation, inside the framework's equation of motion, of the claim that a merely continuous force map suffices for uniqueness of the motion through an initial datum: the unit-mass model in three dimensions with force $F(x)=m\\sqrt{|x_1|}e_1$ is continuous but not state-locally-Lipschitz at the origin, and exhibits two distinct $C^2$ motions through the rest datum. The item refutes only the weakened variant of the force postulate in which continuity replaces the local-Lipschitz clause; it asserts no motion of any physical body, no measurement and no empirical claim."

cex-cm02-singular-collision-finite-time.title: "A singular collision in finite time: the inverse-square external model has a motion whose maximal interval is bounded above"
cex-cm02-singular-collision-finite-time.physical_scope: "A refutation, inside the model, of the claim that every motion of the inverse-square external-potential model exists for all real times: for one label of mass $m>0$ in the external potential $U(x)=-k/|x|$ on the collision-excluded domain, an explicit radial motion with the stated initial data solves the model on $(-\\infty,T)$ and has no extension past the finite time $T$, at which the position reaches the excluded center and the speed is unbounded. The item refutes only the all-time-existence claim for this model, illustrates the escape alternative of the breakdown criterion, and asserts no motion of any physical body, no measurement and no empirical claim."

cex-cm03-centrality-is-not-necessary-for.title: "Non-central antisymmetric pair forces with vanishing internal torque sum: the centrality clause is not necessary for angular-momentum conservation"
cex-cm03-centrality-is-not-necessary-for.physical_scope: "A counterexample inside the force branch: a three-label model with constant antisymmetric pair forces has non-central pair forces and yet its internal torque sum vanishes identically, so its total angular momentum about a fixed origin is constant along every motion even though the centrality hypothesis of the balance theorem fails. The item refutes only the claim that centrality is necessary for the internal-torque conclusion; it asserts no measured value and no conservation for general non-central models."

cex-cm03-closed-force-field-without-a-gl.title: "A closed (curl-free) model force field on an annular domain with no global potential energy: mechanical energy is available only locally"
cex-cm03-closed-force-field-without-a-gl.physical_scope: "A counterexample inside the potential branch: on a declared open annular configuration domain a smooth time- and velocity-independent force field is closed (curl-free) and yet has no global potential energy, so the model is not a global potential model, no global mechanical energy of the framework's form exists, and the energy-conservation hypothesis of the balance theorem cannot be replaced by closedness; on every star-shaped subdomain a local potential and a locally conserved mechanical energy do exist. The item asserts no measured value and no global conservation."

cex-cm04-undamped-resonance-with-bounded.title: "A bounded sinusoidal drive with unbounded motions: the undamped driven oscillator at $\\Omega=\\omega_0$ refutes the unqualified boundedness claim"
cex-cm04-undamped-resonance-with-bounded.physical_scope: "A counterexample inside the driven oscillator model: with m=k=1, zero damping, drive amplitude 1 N and drive frequency equal to the natural frequency, the drive is bounded and yet the model has an unbounded motion (indeed every motion is unbounded), so the unqualified claim that a bounded prescribed drive forces bounded motions is false. The contrast with the strictly damped parameter c=1/5 (every motion bounded) and with the undamped off-resonant frequency Omega=2 (every motion bounded) shows the failure is exactly the zero-damping resonant case. The item asserts no measured value and no claim about any apparatus."

cex-cm05-external-force-breaks-relative-.title: "External forces break the two-body reduction: a two-label model with a static central pair potential and external forces $\\pm\\gamma$ has $\\mu r''=\\gamma\\ne0$, although its total external force vanishes"
cex-cm05-external-force-breaks-relative-.physical_scope: "A refutation of the unconditional two-body reduction: an explicit two-label force model with the external-plus-pair presentation, a (zero) static central pair potential and antisymmetric constant external forces has an explicit motion whose relative coordinate is not a central-force trajectory, even though the total external force and the centre-of-mass balance are unaffected. The item is a finite check inside the adopted force branch; it asserts no observation and identifies only the necessity of the no-external-force hypothesis of the reduction theorem."

cex-cm11-invariants-do-not-force-uniform.title: "A torque-free motion of a symmetric rigid-material model with constant angular momentum and energy whose body angular velocity is not constant: the invariants do not force a uniform rotation"
cex-cm11-invariants-do-not-force-uniform.physical_scope: "A refutation inside the torque-free branch of the rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]]: on the declared symmetric model with body inertia matrix diag(1,1,2) there is a torque-free motion whose angular momentum about the centre of mass and rotational kinetic energy are both constant while its body angular velocity varies with time. The item refutes only the displayed false statement; it asserts no measurement, no concrete body and no failure of the torque-free equations, of which the exhibited motion is an exact solution."

cex-cm14-free-particle-noncompact-fibre.title: "A free label: a nonempty regular common level set of a completely integrable datum that is noncompact and has no period lattice"
cex-cm14-free-particle-noncompact-fibre.physical_scope: "A counterexample inside the zero-force potential presentation of the framework's force branch: the one-label free datum $(H)$ with $H=|p|^2/(2m)$ on the Cartesian phase domain is a completely integrable datum, and its positive-energy common level set is a nonempty regular level set that is unbounded, hence noncompact, and on which the Hamiltonian flow is free with trivial stabilizer, so no nonzero period and no full period lattice exist. The item asserts no measured value and no claim about any apparatus; it shows that compactness cannot be dropped from the torus and period-lattice conclusions."

cex-cm14-harmonic-model-critical-fibre.title: "The zero-energy level of the harmonic model: a compact connected common level set of a completely integrable datum that is a point, not a torus"
cex-cm14-harmonic-model-critical-fibre.physical_scope: "A counterexample inside the declared harmonic model of the framework's force branch: the one-label harmonic datum $(H)$ on the whole Cartesian phase plane is a completely integrable datum, and its zero common level set is compact, connected and nonempty but consists of the single rest point, so it is not diffeomorphic to a torus; equivalently, the level is a critical level at which the regular-fibre hypotheses of the torus theorem fail. The item asserts no measured value and no claim about any apparatus; it shows that regularity cannot be dropped from the hypotheses."

cex-cm15-deflection-need-not-decrease.title: "Smooth finite-range free scattering refutes global strict decrease; as a separate contact comparison, an attractive refracting shell with index $3/2$ has $\\theta(b)=2(\\arcsin(b/a)-\\arcsin(2b/(3a)))$ strictly increasing, with a jump down to $0$ at grazing incidence"
cex-cm15-deflection-need-not-decrease.physical_scope: "The smooth finite-range model has zero deflection for every impact parameter beyond its range, so any globally defined deflection map is constant on this tail and cannot be strictly decreasing. The zero potential is a genuine smooth witness with unique deflection for every positive impact parameter. As a separate model comparison, the adopted attractive refracting shell of index 3/2 retains its strictly increasing deflection on 0<b<a and its declared grazing jump to zero; it is outside the smooth central-scattering class. All computations concern declared model data and report no observations."

cex-cm15-momentum-alone-does-not-fix-the.title: "Reciprocal impulses do not determine a collinear impact: the same incoming data admit the sticking outcome $v^+=0$ and the elastic outcome $(v_1^+,v_2^+)=(-3,1)\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ with different impulses and energies"
cex-cm15-momentum-alone-does-not-fix-the.physical_scope: "A refutation of the claim that the reciprocal impulse equations alone determine a collinear impact: with masses $2$ and $6\\,\\mathrm{kg}$ and incoming velocities $3$ and $-1\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$, both the sticking outcome and the elastic outcome satisfy the equal-and-opposite momentum jumps with impulses $-6\\,\\mathrm{N\\,s}$ and $-12\\,\\mathrm{N\\,s}$ respectively and total momentum $0$, while velocities and kinetic-energy changes differ. Hence the contact law fixing the impulse (or the coefficient of restitution) is an independent model datum. The witness uses declared model data and asserts no measurement, no determination of any real coefficient and no observation."

cex-cm15-restitution-above-one-increases.title: "A coefficient of restitution above $1$ manufactures kinetic energy: $e=2$ on $m_1=m_2=1\\,\\mathrm{kg}$ with velocities $\\pm1\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ raises the kinetic energy by $3\\,\\mathrm{J}$ while the configuration is unchanged"
cex-cm15-restitution-above-one-increases.physical_scope: "A refutation of the claim that every real coefficient of restitution is admissible in the adopted isolated-impact model: with the collinear restitution law and $e=2$ on declared data, the kinetic energy rises by $3\\,\\mathrm{J}$ across an impact while the configuration is instantaneously unchanged, so the total mechanical energy of a conservative two-label model is not conserved; values $e>1$ therefore signal an omitted internal energy reservoir and are excluded from the conservative contact model of this page, which restricts $e$ to $[0,1]$. The witness uses declared model data and asserts no measurement."

cex-cm16-positive-growth-is-not-chaos.title: "A positive Lyapunov exponent at a hyperbolic equilibrium does not produce a chaotic invariant set: the repulsive linear model has rate $1$ at its equilibrium and no compact invariant set with more than one point"
cex-cm16-positive-growth-is-not-chaos.physical_scope: "A declared-model counterexample refuting the implication from a positive Lyapunov exponent at an equilibrium to the existence of a chaotic compact invariant set: the dimensionless repulsive linear model U(q)=-q^2/2 has the positive exponent 1 at its equilibrium along the unstable direction, its equilibrium is nonlinearly unstable, and yet every compact invariant set of its flow is the single point {0}, which fails the sensitivity clause of the page's chaos list. The counterexample is a model computation; it reports no measurement."

cex-cm16-stability-does-not-imply-attrac.title: "Lyapunov stability does not imply attraction: the harmonic model is stable at its equilibrium while every nonzero datum keeps its distance and never converges"
cex-cm16-stability-does-not-imply-attrac.physical_scope: "A declared-model counterexample refuting the implication from Lyapunov stability to asymptotic stability for the page's mechanical models: the one-dimensional harmonic model with unit mass and unit stiffness has the equilibrium 0, which is Lyapunov stable by the strict-minimum theorem, while the datum (delta,0) has the periodic motion delta cos(t) whose distance from the equilibrium returns to delta at every period, so it never converges. The counterexample is a model computation; it reports no measurement."

cex-cm17-traction-symmetry-without-stres.title: "FALSE: the reversed-normal convention alone makes a continuous traction field a stress matrix. The field t(n)=|n_1|n refutes it"

cex-cm18-finite-sample-may-miss-the-sign.title: "A finite sample can miss a predicted outcome with positive probability: an elementary product-model counterexample"
cex-cm18-finite-sample-may-miss-the-sign.physical_scope: "A counterexample to a stated inference rule for finite samples: it exhibits a finite probability model, of the product form used for independent repetitions, in which a designated outcome occurs with probability p in (0,1) at every trial while a finite sample avoids it with probability (1-p)^n in (0,1). The item refutes only the implication from a finite sample without the outcome to the falsehood of the declared sampling model; it asserts no experiment, no observed sequence and nothing about the truth or falsity of any physical model."

def-cm-constrained-configuration-and-mas.title: "Constrained configurations, the mass matrix and the mass metric"

def-cm-traction-and-stress.title: "Traction fields and stress matrices representing them"

def-cm01-configuration.title: "Configuration domain of $N$ labeled particles: open admissible sets, regular holonomic constraints and the mass operator"
def-cm01-configuration.physical_scope: "Definition of the configuration stage of the framework: for $N$ labeled particles of the model, the admissible position tuples in one inertial frame as an open set or as the regular zero set of holonomic constraint functions, the collision exclusion of a singular force model, the degree-of-freedom count, and the mass operator assembled from the fixed masses. The item defines vocabulary only; it adopts no force law, no equation of motion and no constitutive assumption, and it asserts no measured value."

def-cm02-newtonian-flow.title: "The associated first-order system, motions, maximal motions and the Newtonian flow of a force model"
def-cm02-newtonian-flow.physical_scope: "Vocabulary of the force branch: the state space of positions and velocities, the inverse-mass operator, the associated first-order system of the second-order equation of motion, motions as its solutions, initial data, the maximal motion and its maximal interval, and the Newtonian flow map. The item defines objects only; it asserts no force law beyond the cited postulate, no regularity of the flow beyond what the cited existence theorems provide, and no empirical claim."

def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta.title: "Total mass, total momentum, centre of mass, angular momentum, torque, kinetic energy, power and work of a particle model in an inertial frame"
def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta.physical_scope: "Vocabulary and dimension conventions for the mechanical quantities of a force model in one inertial frame: the total mass, total momentum, centre of mass, relative positions and centre-of-mass velocity; the angular momentum, total torque, external torque and internal torque sum about a reference curve; the kinetic energy, the power of the total force and the work over a time interval. The item defines these symbols from the model's particles and force map and fixes their frames; it asserts no balance, no conservation law and no measured value."

def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy.title: "Potential presentations of a force model, potential and mechanical energy, closed versus exact force fields, local potentials and equipotential level sets"
def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy.physical_scope: "The potential branch of the force model: a scalar potential representing the force map through the Euclidean gradient, with or without declared residual forces; the potential and mechanical energy along a curve family; the non-uniqueness of the potential under addition of a function of time; the distinction between closed and exact time- and velocity-independent force fields, with local potentials on star-shaped subdomains and the failure of global exactness on a punctured domain; and equipotential level sets. The item defines the branch and records cited mathematical facts; it asserts no conservation law, no measured value and no global potential for an arbitrary closed field."

def-cm04-one-dimensional-models-and-equi.title: "The one-dimensional force models: data, motions, phase system, potential presentation, energy and equilibria"
def-cm04-one-dimensional-models-and-equi.physical_scope: "The declared one-dimensional model class of the framework: a single scalar coordinate with an open configuration interval, a fixed positive mass, and a scalar force law with the standing continuity and state-Lipschitz regularity; the motions, the phase system, the potential presentation with a scalar potential and residual forces, the mechanical energy, the equilibria of a time- and velocity-independent force law, and the oscillator-type data (m,c,k,f). The item fixes vocabulary, domains, regularity and dimensions for the conservative and dissipative models of this page; it adopts no force law of nature, asserts no existence, uniqueness, conservation or stability statement, and records no measured value."

def-cm04-phase-plane-and-energy-level-se.title: "The phase plane of a one-dimensional model: phase curves, the energy function and its level sets, and turning points"
def-cm04-phase-plane-and-energy-level-se.physical_scope: "The geometric vocabulary of the one-dimensional models of this page: the phase plane with its position and velocity coordinates, the phase curve of a motion, the mechanical energy function of a conservative model, its energy level sets and sublevel sets, and turning positions and turning points. The item also fixes how the equilibrium, Lyapunov-stability and linear-stability vocabulary of the mathematical definitions is read for the scalar phase system. It asserts no conservation, no containment of phase curves in level sets, no boundedness and no measured value; those are statements of the theorems of this page."

def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model.title: "Holonomic-constraint models of the force branch: constraint data, the constrained equation, virtual displacements and the scleronomic/rheonomic distinction"
def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model.physical_scope: "Definition of the holonomic-constraint branch of the force model: the declared regular constraint map on an ambient set, the constraint locus and its instantaneous configuration manifolds, constrained curve families and permitted velocities, the virtual displacements, the reaction field and the constrained equation of motion, the consistent initial data, and the scleronomic/rheonomic classification of the constraint locus. The item declares a model class; it adopts no ideal-reaction law, no force law beyond the force branch and no measured value, and it does not assert that any real mechanism is described by the class."

def-cm06-nonholonomic-model.title: "Velocity-constraint (nonholonomic) models of the force branch: constant-rank constraint laws, the d'Alembert reaction and holonomic equivalence"
def-cm06-nonholonomic-model.physical_scope: "Definition of the velocity-constraint branch of the force model: a declared constant-rank affine velocity law, its admissible velocities and Chetaev virtual displacements at frozen time and configuration, kinematically admissible curve families, the adopted d'Alembert ideal-reaction law and its multiplier representation, the equation of the branch, the classification of holonomic equivalence and nonholonomic models, and the exclusion of rank changes, contact changes, impacts, friction and driving. The item defines a model class; it asserts no measured value and does not claim that any particular mechanism is described by it."

def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangia.title: "The action functional of a force model with a potential presentation: the mechanical Lagrangian, its chart instance and its dimensions"
def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangia.physical_scope: "The action functional of the framework's force branch with a declared potential presentation: the kinetic energy of the labels in an inertial frame, the mechanical Lagrangian K - U of the presentation, the open chart and the action integral over C^2 curves with fixed endpoints, the first variation and stationarity, and the dimensions of these objects. The item defines model-derived objects only: it asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law, no minimisation property and no empirical value, and it does not claim that any apparatus is described by a Lagrangian or by the potential branch."

def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-for.title: "Generalized-coordinate maps of the model, the substituted Lagrangian, the kinetic metric and generalized forces"
def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-for.physical_scope: "The dictionary from the model's Cartesian description to generalized coordinates: a C^3 configuraton map that is an immersion (a chart when the coordinate count equals 3N, a parametrisation of a regular holonomic-constraint locus when it does not), the substituted Lagrangian with its kinetic metric, the generalized force of a declared force contribution as the Jacobian-transpose multiple, and the declared Lagrange equations with residual generalized forces. The item defines objects and a model class only; it asserts no equivalence with the constrained equation of motion, which is the reduction theorem of this page, and no empirical claim."

def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagr.title: "Continuous symmetries of the model's mechanical Lagrangian: symmetry data, the Noether identity, the charge and its dimensions"
def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagr.physical_scope: "The symmetry vocabulary of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: symmetry data as triples (tau, xi, B) satisfying the model's Noether identity for the mechanical Lagrangian K - U, strict data and their exact relation to the chart-level infinitesimal point symmetries, the charge M v . xi - (K+U) tau - B together with its dimension and its behaviour under rescaling of the family parameter, and the status of the notion. The item defines only; it asserts no conservation law, no existence of any symmetry of a given model, and no empirical content."

def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model.title: "The coupled quadratic oscillator model: mass metric, stiffness, generalized force, modal vocabulary and the small-oscillation model at a mechanical equilibrium"
def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model.physical_scope: "The restricted model class used on this page: a constant mass metric matrix M (symmetric positive definite) and a constant symmetric stiffness matrix K in a chart of n coordinate directions, with an optional prescribed generalized force J(t), and the model equation M q'' + K q = J(t); together with the quadratic kinetic and potential energies, the phase system, the modal vocabulary of the decoupling transform, and the small-oscillation model assigned to a mechanical equilibrium q_0 of a chart mechanical system, whose mass metric is M(q_0) and whose stiffness is the potential Hessian D^2 U(q_0). The item declares vocabulary, domains, regularity and dimensions only; it asserts no existence, uniqueness, conservation, stability, resonance or approximation statement, adopts no force law of nature, records no measured value, and states no empirical applicability. In particular the mass metric and the stiffness are model parameters of the declared chart, not measured quantities, and the quadratic model is an idealization whose accuracy near an equilibrium is quantified only by the approximation theorems of this page."

def-cm12-cotangent-momentum.title: "The momentum of a potential presentation: the fibre derivative of the mechanical Lagrangian, the Cartesian momentum Mv and generalized momenta"
def-cm12-cotangent-momentum.physical_scope: "The momentum datum of the framework's force branch with a declared potential presentation: the Cartesian momentum Mv of the labelled particles in an inertial frame, its identification with the fibre derivative of the mechanical Lagrangian, the generalized momenta G(q)v of a declared generalized-coordinate map, their dimensions and their pairings with velocities. The item defines model-derived objects only: it asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law, no inverse-Legendre branch and no measured value, and it does not claim that any apparatus is described by the potential branch."

def-cm12-hamiltonian.title: "The Hamiltonian of a hyperregular potential presentation: the Legendre transform of the mechanical Lagrangian, its domain and its dimensions"
def-cm12-hamiltonian.physical_scope: "The Hamiltonian datum of a hyperregular potential presentation: the Legendre transform p.v - L evaluated on the declared inverse Legendre branch, in Cartesian data and in a declared generalized-coordinate chart, its momentum phase domain, its energy dimension and its dependence on the declared chart, branch and potential representative. The item defines a model-derived function only; it asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law and no measured value, and the explicit kinetic-plus-potential form for the mechanical branch is a theorem of this page, not part of the definition."

def-cm12-hyperregularity.title: "Hyperregular potential presentations and their inverse Legendre branches in the model's charts"
def-cm12-hyperregularity.physical_scope: "Hyperregularity of a potential presentation of the force branch and the vocabulary of its inverse Legendre branch: invertibility of the fibrewise velocity-to-momentum map, the globally defined inverse branch and its momentum phase chart in Cartesian data and in a declared generalized-coordinate chart. The item defines a condition on the model's declared chart data and the branch objects used by the Hamiltonian definition; it asserts neither that the model's presentations satisfy the condition nor any equation of motion, conservation law or measured value."

def-cm12-regularity.title: "Velocity-regular potential presentations: the velocity Hessian of the mechanical Lagrangian, regular states and regular charts"
def-cm12-regularity.physical_scope: "The regularity vocabulary of a potential presentation of the framework's force branch: the velocity Hessian of the mechanical Lagrangian in Cartesian data and in a declared generalized-coordinate chart, velocity-regular states and regular presentations, and the local inverse branch data attached to a regular state. The item defines conditions on the model's chart data and fixes the notation used by the local Legendre theorem and by the Hamiltonian items; it asserts no existence of a global momentum inverse, no equation of motion and no measured value."

def-cm13-canonical-form.title: "Canonical coordinates and the canonical form of the two-form for a potential presentation: the coordinate expression $\\omega=\\sum d\\theta^a\\wedge d\\theta^{n+a}$ and the model's own momentum charts"
def-cm13-canonical-form.physical_scope: "The vocabulary of canonical coordinates for the two-form of a declared potential presentation: coordinates on a phase domain in which the presentation's two-form takes the canonical coordinate expression, and the record that the presentation's Cartesian momentum chart and each of its generalized-coordinate momentum charts are canonical charts. The item defines a coordinate condition and fixes the vocabulary used by the bracket, field, flow and generating-function items; it asserts no dynamics, no existence of canonical coordinates beyond the model's own charts and no measured value."

def-cm13-canonical-map.title: "Canonical maps of a potential presentation: maps preserving the two-form, their determinant tests, the transport of Hamiltonian fields, and the model's listed canonical maps"
def-cm13-canonical-map.physical_scope: "The canonical-map datum of a declared potential presentation: $C^{1}$ maps between open subsets of the presentation's phase domains which pull the two-form back to itself, the determinant test on their Jacobians, the transport identity for Hamiltonian fields, and the record that the model's chart transitions, flow maps and generating-function maps are canonical. The item defines the model's canonical transformations and fixes the tests used throughout this page and by its consumers; it asserts no existence of canonical maps beyond the listed suppliers and no measured value."

def-cm13-hamiltonian-field.title: "The Hamiltonian field of a phase function for a potential presentation: the unique field $X_f$ with $\\iota_{X_f}\\omega=df$, and $X_H=(H_p,-H_x)$ for the branch Hamiltonian"
def-cm13-hamiltonian-field.physical_scope: "The Hamiltonian field datum of a declared potential presentation: for a $C^{2}$ phase function the unique $C^{1}$ field contracted against the presentation's two-form to the differential, together with its coordinate expression in the model's Cartesian and generalized-coordinate charts and its specialization to the branch Hamiltonian, including the residual-force source that is generally not a Hamiltonian field. The item defines model fields and their chart expressions; it asserts no existence of integral curves, no equation of motion and no measured value."

def-cm13-poisson.title: "The Poisson bracket of phase functions of a potential presentation: $\\{f,g\\}=\\omega(X_f,X_g)$ and the coordinate formula in each canonical chart"
def-cm13-poisson.physical_scope: "The Poisson bracket datum of a declared potential presentation: phase functions read off the labels' positions and momenta, the bracket $\\{f,g\\}=\\omega(X_f,X_g)$ defined by the presentation's two-form, and its coordinate formula in the model's Cartesian and generalized-coordinate canonical charts. The item defines a model bilinear operation and fixes its dimension; it asserts no algebraic identity, no equation of motion, no conservation law and no measured value."

def-cm13-two-form.title: "The canonical one-form and the two-form of a potential presentation: $\\lambda=p\\cdot dx$ on the Cartesian momentum phase chart and the induced forms on each generalized-coordinate chart"
def-cm13-two-form.physical_scope: "The symplectic data of a potential presentation of the framework's force branch: on the Cartesian momentum phase chart $Q\\times\\mathbb R^{3N}$ the canonical one-form $\\lambda=p\\cdot\\delta x$ and the two-form $\\omega=-d\\lambda$, and on each declared generalized-coordinate momentum chart the forms pulled back along the presentation's own chart map $(q,P)\\mapsto(X(q),\\mathsf M\\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}P)$. The item defines model objects of the declared presentation and its declared chart only; it asserts no closedness, nondegeneracy, dynamics or measured value, and it fixes the sign convention $\\iota_X\\omega=dH$ used throughout this page."

def-cm14-complete-integrability.title: "Completely integrable data of a declared presentation: $n$ smooth phase functions with $F_1=H$, pairwise in involution and independent on the regular locus"
def-cm14-complete-integrability.physical_scope: "Complete integrability of the Hamiltonian system of a declared hyperregular potential presentation: a datum of $n$ phase functions on an open phase domain of dimension $2n$, with first entry the branch Hamiltonian, pairwise in involution, independent on an open dense regular locus, and the attached integral map, regular values and regular fibres; the datum is a completely integrable Hamiltonian system for the presentation's two-form in the root-library sense. The item defines the datum class; it asserts no model of the force branch is completely integrable, no fibre structure, no action-angle coordinates and no measured value."

def-cm14-complete-integral.title: "A complete integral of the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation: nondegenerate mixed derivative, momentum map and Jacobi constants"
def-cm14-complete-integral.physical_scope: "The complete-integral datum of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: a $C^3$ solution $S$ of the presentation's Hamilton-Jacobi equation in a fixed momentum chart whose mixed derivative $S_{q\\alpha}$ is invertible at the base point, together with its momentum map $p=S_q$ and its Jacobi constants $\\beta=S_\\alpha$, their dimensions and their reading as a family of model data labelled by the parameters $\\alpha$. The item defines the datum only; the constancy of the Jacobi constants along the characteristic motions, the local solvability of the constants equation and the canonicity of $(\\beta,\\alpha)$ are theorems of this page, not part of the definition, and no existence or measured value is asserted."

def-cm14-hamilton-jacobi-equation.title: "The Hamilton-Jacobi equation of a declared potential presentation: the class of action-dimension functions $S$ with $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$ in one momentum chart"
def-cm14-hamilton-jacobi-equation.physical_scope: "The Hamilton-Jacobi equation of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch, read in one of the presentation's momentum charts: the class of $C^3$ functions $S$ of the chart variables $(t,q,\\alpha)$ that satisfy $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$ for the branch Hamiltonian $H$ of that chart, together with the action dimension of $S$ and the dependence of the equation on the declared chart, inverse Legendre branch and potential representative. The item defines a function class relative to that datum; it asserts no existence of solutions, no equation of motion for the model, no completeness of any flow and no measured value."

def-cm14-involution.title: "First integrals of the model's Hamiltonian and families in involution: the bracket criterion and differential independence"
def-cm14-involution.physical_scope: "First integrals and involution for the Hamiltonian system of a declared hyperregular potential presentation of the framework's force branch: phase functions on an open phase domain that are constant along the model's motions, their bracket criterion with the branch Hamiltonian, families of phase functions in involution, and the differential independence of a family on the regular region. The item defines these model properties; it asserts no existence of integrals, no conservation law for a particular force law and no measured value."

def-cm15-asymptotic-data.title: "Scattering data of the central model class: the scattering motion, the impact parameter, the asymptotic directions, the deflection conventions and the uniform-incident preparation"
def-cm15-asymptotic-data.physical_scope: "The physical reading of the scattering data of the page's restricted model class: the two-label central model of the central-model postulate, its reduced problem, the scattering motion of the relative coordinate on all of R, the energy and angular momentum carried by the motion, the asymptotic velocities, the impact parameter as the perpendicular distance of the incoming branch, the polar advance and the deflection conventions, the adopted uniform-incident preparation and its flux and units, and the reading conventions (angles are relative-frame angles) together with the explicit exclusions and the status of the data as model data. The item fixes vocabulary and an adopted preparation model; it asserts no observation, no measured value, no law of nature and no counting of detected particles."

def-cm15-cross-section.title: "The differential and truncated total cross-sections of a deflection branch: densities, units, branch sums and the empirical qualifications of the uniform-incident reading"
def-cm15-cross-section.physical_scope: "The page's cross-section vocabulary for the uniform-incident preparation: the differential cross-section as the area-pushforward density of a deflection branch of a central scattering model, its units, the branch-sum convention, the truncated total cross-section over an angular window with finite or singular endpoints, and the empirical qualifications of the uniform-incident reading (adopted preparation, model rates not detections, finite samples, detector acceptance, no ideal total for a forward-divergent branch). The item defines model quantities; it asserts no observation, no measured value and no counting of detected particles."

def-cm16-chaos-list-for-model-maps.title: "Chaos in the stated sense for maps of the model: topological mixing, dense periodic points and sensitive dependence, as one precise list among several"
def-cm16-chaos-list-for-model-maps.physical_scope: "The chaos vocabulary of the page, applied to the stroboscopic and Poincare return maps of the declared models: a continuous map of a metric space is chaotic in the stated sense when it is topologically mixing, has dense periodic points and has sensitive dependence on initial conditions with a positive constant, with the three predicates spelled out exactly. The item fixes one precise list among several used in the literature, requires an invariant set and a metric relative to which the properties are stated, and asserts no measure-theoretic property, no entropy or dimension and no empirical claim."

def-cm16-finite-time-growth-rates.title: "Finite-time tangent growth rates and Lyapunov exponents of the model's flow: the rate per unit time of a transported deviation, with its existence convention and its limits"
def-cm16-finite-time-growth-rates.physical_scope: "The finite-time tangent growth rate and, when the limit exists, the Lyapunov exponent of a declared autonomy model whose force map is of class C1 in the state: the rate is the logarithm per unit time of the Euclidean norm of a nonzero transported deviation vector, and the exponent is assigned only when the limit over the declared time interval exists. The item fixes the definition, its dependence on the chart and norm, and the boundaries of what the rate does and does not assert (positive finite-time growth is not chaos, not instability of a trajectory and not an invariant of a change of coordinates)."

def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-s.title: "The model vocabulary of stability and chaos: the associated flow of a declared force model, equilibria, periodic and homoclinic orbits, and invariant sets"
def-cm16-flow-equilibria-and-invariant-s.physical_scope: "The model vocabulary of the page's stability, perturbation and chaos statements: the autonomous force models of the framework (open configuration domain, fixed positive masses, a continuous state-locally-Lipschitz force map), their associated first-order fields and local flows with maximal solutions, equilibrium states (vanishing force at rest), periodic orbits and limit cycles, invariant and forward-invariant sets, orbital distance, and homoclinic and heteroclinic orbits as limit relations of motions. All objects are declared model data; the item asserts no measurement, no existence of any particular equilibrium or periodic orbit, and no stability of any of the listed objects."

def-cm16-stability-and-hyperbolicity-con.title: "Stability vocabulary of the model: Lyapunov, asymptotic and orbital stability, linear stability of equilibria and periodic orbits, and hyperbolicity of equilibria and fixed points"
def-cm16-stability-and-hyperbolicity-con.physical_scope: "The stability predicates attached to the model vocabulary of the page: Lyapunov stability and asymptotic stability of an equilibrium state with their exact quantifiers over maximal solutions, orbital stability of a compact invariant set, linear stability of an equilibrium through bounded solutions of the variational equation, linear stability of a periodic orbit through bounded iterates of the derivative of a return map, and hyperbolicity of an equilibrium of the model's field and of a fixed point of a C1 map (spectra off the imaginary axis or the unit circle). The item records the distinctions between these notions and asserts no stability, instability or attraction of any particular model."

def-cm16-stroboscopic-and-poincare-maps.title: "The stroboscopic map of a periodic model and the Poincare return map of a transversal section: domains, iterates, fixed points and the local C1 diffeomorphism property"
def-cm16-stroboscopic-and-poincare-maps.physical_scope: "The two maps used to reduce the model's dynamics to discrete time: the stroboscopic map at the period of a P-periodic force model, defined only on states whose motion exists over the full period, with iterates recursively defined and fixed points in bijection with P-periodic motions; and the local Poincare return map of a transversal section of an autonomous model, whose existence, C1 regularity and local invertibility are supplied from the first-return mapping theorem. The item asserts no completeness, no global return and no all-time existence of iterates."

def-cm17-traction-and-stress.title: "Traction fields and stress matrices of the continuum model, with units and sign conventions"
def-cm17-traction-and-stress.physical_scope: "The model's contact-force quantity: a traction field assigning to each point and unit normal the force per unit area exerted across a surface, its dimensions, and the stress matrix representing it when one exists; the sign convention identifying compressive normal traction with negative scalar stress, the component reading, and the distinction from body-force densities. Existence of a representing stress matrix, its continuity and its symmetry are not asserted here; they are conditional conclusions of the balance items of this page. No measured force is asserted."

def-cm18-calibration.title: "Calibration of a mechanical apparatus against the primitive standards of the framework: reference inputs, deviations, rules and calibrated prediction maps"
def-cm18-calibration.physical_scope: "Calibration of an apparatus for an operational observable model of the force branch: a family of prediction maps indexed by apparatus settings, a finite family of reference inputs traced to realizations of the framework's primitive quantities (durations in seconds, lengths in metres, masses in kilograms) with declared deviations, declared reference observations and a calibration rule. The item defines the datum that assigns numerical values in the framework's units to model parameters; it asserts no accuracy, consistency or unbiasedness of any calibration, no realized standard and no measurement."

def-cm18-observable-model.title: "Operational observable model of the force branch: parameters, preparations, observation times, readout, units and additive error"
def-cm18-observable-model.physical_scope: "Operational observable models of an adopted force model: a parameter set indexing force maps, a preparation map assigning initial data, a finite family of observation times lying in the maximal motions, a declared readout of the model states, declared units for the readout coordinates, a probability space and an additive error random element with values in a declared open error domain. The item fixes the interface between the force branch and the measurement-model machinery of the companion mathematics page; it asserts no distributional, moment, independence or calibration hypothesis, no apparatus realization and no measurement, and it does not claim that any physical situation satisfies the protocol."

def-cm18-sampling-model.title: "Repeated-observation protocols of the force branch: adopted IID and second-moment sampling hypotheses and the sample mean"
def-cm18-sampling-model.physical_scope: "Repeated-observation protocols with a scalar readout for an operational observable model of the force branch: a repetition count, one error random element per repetition on a common probability space, the resulting observations, and the adopted IID and second-moment hypotheses on the repeated preparation. The item records what the sampling hypotheses assume about repetitions and what follows for the sample mean by the cited mathematical supplier; it does not assert that any physical sequence of repetitions satisfies the hypotheses and reports no observed value."

ex-cm-couette-poiseuille-numbers.title: "Numerical checks for channel flows: $h=\\eta=1$, $G=12$ gives flux $1$ and centre speed $3/2$, and $V=2$ gives shear $2$"

ex-cm-mass-metric-on-a-sphere.title: "The mass metric of a particle constrained to the unit sphere in spherical coordinates"

ex-cm01-dimension-bookkeeping.title: "Dimension bookkeeping for the quantities and frame parameters of the framework page"
ex-cm01-dimension-bookkeeping.physical_scope: "A worked application of the dimension conventions of the framework to the quantities and frame parameters of this page: the dimensions of time and position coordinates, velocity, acceleration, mass, the mass operator, the Galilean parameters and the displayed transformation laws are computed from the convention rules and checked for consistency. The item asserts no measured value and no law of nature; it is bookkeeping inside the stated conventions."

ex-cm01-two-particle-rigid-rod-configura.title: "Configuration domains of two labeled particles: collision exclusion and a rigid rod as a regular holonomic constraint"
ex-cm01-two-particle-rigid-rod-configura.physical_scope: "A worked verification for two labeled particles of the model: openness of the collision-excluded configuration domain, and the rigid-rod holonomic constraint as a regular level set of the squared-distance function with five configuration degrees of freedom and the two-particle mass operator. The example is a computation inside the definition of the configuration stage; it adopts no force law, asserts no motion and contains no empirical claim."

ex-cm02-constant-field-projectile.title: "Projectile motion in the constant-field model: planar parabolic trajectory, flight time and level range for stated model data"
ex-cm02-constant-field-projectile.physical_scope: "A worked computation inside the constant-field model of [[ex-cm02-uniform-field]]: for a stated initial position, speed and launch angle and a declared constant field parameter, the trajectory is planar and parabolic, the return-to-launch-height time and the level range are computed from the model, and the motion is the unique maximal motion through the datum. The item asserts no measured value of any field strength or launch parameter, models no medium and no drag, and records that the constant-field description of a realistic field is an approximation."

ex-cm02-drag-terminal-velocity.title: "Motion under linear drag and a constant applied force: explicit global solution and approach to the terminal velocity"
ex-cm02-drag-terminal-velocity.physical_scope: "A worked computation inside the linear drag model of [[post-cm02-drag]] with a constant applied force: for a stated initial position and velocity the explicit motion is verified, it is the unique maximal motion and exists for all real times, and its velocity converges to the terminal velocity $(m/c)\\mathbf g$ with an explicit exponential bound. The item is a conditional computation inside the model; the coefficient and field parameters are declared model data, no measured value is asserted, and the phenomenological and regime qualifications of the drag postulate are preserved."

ex-cm02-force-model-regularity-checks.title: "Standing regularity of the page's force models checked: uniform field, linear drag and the inverse-square model on its collision-excluded domain"
ex-cm02-force-model-regularity-checks.physical_scope: "A worked model check inside the framework: verification that three force maps of this page satisfy the standing continuity and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses of the force postulate, with explicit constants where available; the uniform-force model has constant 0, the linear drag model has constant c, and the inverse-square external model is locally Lipschitz on each collision-free annulus with the stated constant and has no continuous extension to the excluded center. The item is a finite verification inside the adopted models; it asserts no motion, no measurement and no empirical claim."

ex-cm02-uniform-field.title: "The uniform-force model: explicit global motion of a label under a constant declared field, with uniqueness, dimensions and frame covariance"
ex-cm02-uniform-field.physical_scope: "A worked verification inside the framework: for one labeled particle of the model, the force map that assigns to every state the same vector $m\\mathbf g$ (a declared constant field parameter of dimension length per time squared) satisfies the standing hypotheses of the force postulate; the explicit quadratic motion solves the initial-value problem, exists on the whole time window, is the unique maximal motion, and the model is covariant under changes of inertial frame with the parameter transforming as a spatial vector. The item is a computation inside the model: it asserts no measured value of any field strength, no property of the Earth's gravitational field and no empirical law, and the constant-field idealization is recorded as an approximation."

ex-cm03-driven-mechanical-energy-balance.title: "A driven one-dimensional model with a time-dependent potential and a residual force: the mechanical-energy balance, the integrated work form and the normalization ambiguity computed on explicit data"
ex-cm03-driven-mechanical-energy-balance.physical_scope: "A worked computation in a declared one-dimensional potential presentation with an explicit time-dependent potential and residual force: the displayed quadratic curve is a motion of the model, and along it the mechanical-energy balance, the power identity, the integrated work form and the change of the energy under a time-dependent renormalization of the potential are computed from the model data. The item asserts no measured value and no conservation; the model is driven."

ex-cm03-two-body-hooke-model-check.title: "A two-body Hooke model with an exact circular relative motion: momentum, kinetic splitting, moving-origin angular momentum, energy conservation and the kinetic boost law checked on explicit data"
ex-cm03-two-body-hooke-model-check.physical_scope: "A worked model check inside the two-body potential branch: for a declared Hooke pair potential with spring constant, mass, separation and centre-of-mass velocity data, the displayed circular relative motion is the unique maximal motion of the model, and along it the total momentum, centre-of-mass motion, kinetic splitting, angular momentum about fixed and moving reference points, mechanical energy and boosted kinetic energy take the values the balance theorems predict. The item asserts no measured value, models no physical spring and claims no empirical agreement."

ex-cm04-damped-regimes-check.title: "The three damping regimes on explicit data: underdamped, critical and overdamped motions at $m=k=1$ and $c=1,2,5$, with their decay bounds"
ex-cm04-damped-regimes-check.physical_scope: "A worked check of the damped oscillator at the declared data m=1 kg, k=1 N/m, datum (0, 1 m, 0 m/s) and the three drag coefficients c=1, 2, 5 kg/s: the three explicit motions of the classification, their initial data, the common initial energy 1/2 J, the strict energy dissipation identity E'=-c x-dot^2, the explicit decay bounds and the convergence to rest. The item asserts no measured value and no claim that a real damper realizes the model."
